rows.en:
I'm telling the first story?
...Okay, what should I talk about?
Oh, before that, let me introduce myself.
My name is Reiko Fukuzawa.
I'm a brand-new first-year, just started here this spring.
Nice to meeeet you, all my seniors!
Umm, you're {c}{f:|}, right?
We're both first-years, but we've never met, have we?
Well, this school is huge.
Or maybe you're always skipping class?
Ahahahaha...
Now that I think about it, I've seen you skipping {f:behind the gym|in the nurse's office}.
Kidding, kidding.
Oh, sorry, sorry.
We're supposed to tell scary stories, right?
Okay then, ready?{p}

Every class has at least one weird kid, right?
I don't mean a kid who gets bullied, or one nobody notices, or anything like that.
They're just different from everyone else somehow.
Something's off about them.
The way they think, the way they act, it's different from everyone else somehow.
Like they're out of focus, or like they're not of this world.
...Hmm, I can't really put it into words.
There's a kid like that in my class too.
My class is Class 1-G, by the way.{p}

Her name is Sanae Motoki.
Sanae is really weird.
Like, in home ec cooking class, you use kitchen knives, right?
When you give Sanae a knife, she just stares and stares at it.
Grinning this creepy grin the whole time.
And then,
"If I stabbed this into my eye, it would really hurt, wouldn't it?"
she mutters, stuff like that.
Those of us watching are totally freaked out, right?
Then she turns the tip of the knife toward herself.
And she stays frozen in that position for a while, just staring.
After that, she lets out a big sigh, and
"Whew, that was scary,"
she says, or something like that.
The whole time, the rest of us were frozen stiff.
We had no idea what was going to happen, so we couldn't move, we just watched in silence.
Then again, if she nicks her finger a little with a knife, she starts bawling her eyes out.
It's not even much blood.
But she cries like it's the end of the world.
I thought something awful had happened. I was more shocked than she was.{p}

And when she eats her lunch, she always prays for over ten minutes before she starts.
I can't tell what she's saying, but she mutters away in a tiny voice, mumble mumble mumble.
Then she bows to her lunch box over and over and over.
And only then does she finally start eating.
Unbelievable, right?
And when she eats, she must chew every bite more than thirty times.
I mean, she eats incredibly slowly.
She uses up the whole lunch break eating.
Then, when she's done, she bows to her lunch box again and starts praying, mumble mumble mumble.
She's a little unhinged, huh?
Kind of scary, right?
But you know, it's not like she's dumb.
She's actually pretty good at studying.
She always ranks near the top on tests and stuff.
And she doesn't get bullied, either.
It kind of bugs me to say it as a girl myself, but she's really cute.
You know, the kind of face everybody likes?
Girls like that have it easy, huh?
Even me, sometimes I find Sanae really irritating, but then I go, 'Oh, whatever,' and forgive her right away.
Actually, we're pretty good friends.
Maybe I'm weird too.
Besides, Sanae may be weird, but she's fun.{p}

The other day, she suddenly started spinning around and around in the classroom, staring up at the ceiling.
"What's wrong?"
I asked her, and she said,
"I'm dizzy and everything's spinning.
So I'm spinning the other way.
If I do that, it'll go away."
That's what she told me.
There's no way that would fix it.
I was just speechless, honestly.
But, like, when Sanae says stuff like that, you can't help laughing.
Isn't there a kid like that in your class too?{p}

But you know, that's not the only weird thing about Sanae.
She had an amazing secret.
And I happened to see that secret by accident.
The other day, when we had P.E., Sanae sat it out because she said she felt sick.
At first she watched the class, but then she said she wanted to lie down and went to the nurse's office.
Her face was deathly pale.{p}

She really did feel sick.
That day in P.E., the girls were playing volleyball.
And I jammed my finger.
Jammed fingers really hurt, right?
So I went to the nurse's office.
And the nurse wasn't there, and Sanae was lying in bed all alone.{p}

She had the blanket pulled up over her head, and she was shaking like crazy.
I couldn't decide whether to say something to her or not.
I mean, she was shaking so hard it looked like the whole bed might start rocking.
Like the bed was about to go wild any second.{p}It felt like I shouldn't say a word to her.
Try calling out to her
Leave her alone for now
Go get the nurse

After all, she's my friend.
I went up to her, meaning to say something.{p}

When I got close, the shaking got even worse, like it was reacting to me.
The bed was scraping across the floor, scrape, scrape.
That's how hard she was shaking.
I got really worried, and I took hold of the blanket.
"Sanae, are you okay?"
No answer.

I figured she hadn't heard me, so I asked again, a little louder.
"Hey, Sanae, are you okay?"
Still no answer.
I didn't know what to do anymore, so I shook her hard by the shoulder.
"Sanae! Sanae!"
I was screaming.
Then a mop of messy hair came poking out of the blanket.
The face was hideously swollen, and the lips, gone purple, were flopped open and curled back.
It was a face you couldn't bear to look at twice.

"Ugh, keep it down. I feel sick, okay?
Can you just leave me alone?"
...It was somebody else.

"What's the matter?"
"Oh, um... I jammed my finger."
The whole time she was treating me, I couldn't settle down.
From the next bed came
"...Geez, seriously. And I've got a fever, too,"
and more sulky grumbling like that.
If he had that bad a fever, he should've just gone home.
I don't go to the nurse's office much, but Ms. Iwasaki, the school nurse, is really kind. She's a good one.
I could kind of see why the boys go out of their way to fake being sick so they can go to the nurse's office.
"There, all better."
After she'd patched me up, I worked up the nerve to ask.
"Um, did Motoki come by here, by any chance?"
"Motoki?"
Ms. Iwasaki gave me a puzzled look.
Well, of course. She doesn't teach our class, so how would she know who someone is just from a name?
"Um, did a girl come in a little while ago, saying she felt sick?
She's in Class 1-G."
Ms. Iwasaki looked troubled.
"...I'm not sure. I stepped out for a bit to take care of something.
Maybe she came in while I was gone."
"Nobody came in."
The sulky-faced guy lying in the bed answered curtly.
Nobody asked him, right?
I bet he's a fan of Ms. Iwasaki too.
That's why he's lying around in the nurse's office instead of going home.
A guy like him is exactly what they mean by 'doesn't know his place.'{p}

But I couldn't figure it out.
If Sanae didn't go to the nurse's office, where on earth had she gone?
What if she'd collapsed somewhere on the way?
I mean, she's the kind of girl who bursts into tears at the sight of a little blood.
So I went looking for Sanae.
But I found her right away.{p}

She was sitting at her own desk in the classroom, all limp.
Maybe she'd headed for the nurse's office, found the nurse wasn't there, and come back to the classroom.
Or maybe she'd never meant to go to the nurse's office at all, and had planned to rest in the classroom from the start.
I didn't know why, but Sanae was sitting at her desk.
Her arms were hanging down limp, her body was slumped against the back of the chair, and her head was flopped back.
She didn't look asleep so much as unconscious.
No, actually, she almost looked dead.
It looked like her eyes had rolled back, showing only the whites.
For a moment, I didn't know what to do, and I just stood there frozen.
I just stared at Sanae, stunned.{p}

Then suddenly, her body jerked up with a jolt.
Just like a puppet on strings, I swear.
She jerked up hard, and then she sat bolt upright.
And then she started slowly rolling her head around and around in a circle.
I tried to cry out, but it was like something had been shoved down my throat. No sound came out.
My body couldn't move either, like I was paralyzed.
I couldn't even look away.{p}

I got such a shock.
Because next, while Sanae sat there bolt upright, still as a wax doll, something like white smoke came out of her mouth.
This hazy stuff kept pouring out of her slack, half-open mouth, more and more of it.
It seemed kind of too solid to be smoke, and it held together strangely.
It was more like cotton.
And then it started taking on a hazy human shape, see?
That's what they call ectoplasm, right?
Even I know that much.
Ectoplasm is a person's soul, isn't it?
Since it came out of Sanae's mouth, I figured it had to be Sanae's soul.
It didn't look the least bit like Sanae's face, but it was a beautiful woman.
A beautiful woman with long hair.
It was just a lump of smoke, but you could clearly make out her features.
See, you're not seeing that with your eyes.
It's a sight you sense with the eye inside your head.
Not your physical eyes, your mind's eye, you know?
That's why you can see it clearly, even though it's smoke.
I don't know the details, but that's what I think.
But the ectoplasm itself is real.
So you see the ectoplasm with your physical eyes, but the face in the smoke you see with your mind's eye.
Too complicated?
So anyway, that ectoplasm looked at me.
Or maybe it's more accurate to say I felt like it looked at me?
But the moment it did, I got the feeling back in my body.
I could breathe easier, and my voice came back.
So then I couldn't decide whether it was okay to say something to Sanae.
I mean, if I called out to her at a time like this and something happened to her, that would be terrible.
But if I just left her like this, there was no guarantee she'd be okay, either.{p}What should I do?
Call out to her
Leave her be

I decided to just watch quietly for the time being.
I mean, wouldn't you?
Ectoplasm was coming out of Sanae's mouth.
If I suddenly called out and gave it a fright, what would happen?
It didn't seem to be doing any harm for now, and if anything happened, I'd jump in right then.
So I just watched without a word.{p}

The ectoplasm stretched and shrank, drifting around for a while.
The thin, threadlike smoke stretching from Sanae's mouth seemed like a lifeline.
Like a baby's umbilical cord, that thin, flimsy thread was holding up the spirit body.
What would happen if it snapped by some accident?
That was the weird thing I was worrying about.
It only lasted a few minutes, but it felt like hours to me.
After a while, Sanae's body shook, jerk, jerk.
And then the ectoplasm got sucked back into Sanae's mouth, slurrrp.
Not all at once, though.
Slowly, slowly, it went in, like it was making sure of the place it was returning to.
In the end, every bit of it went back inside Sanae, without leaving a trace.
And at that exact moment...{p}
Sanae's body lurched again, and she slumped forward.

Sanae banged her head on the desk with a thunk.
That looked like it hurt.
And then, get this.
Sanae stretched and let out this 'Mmmmmm' sound, like someone who's been dragged out of bed in the morning while they're still sleepy.
She really did seem like she'd been asleep. She was rubbing her puffy eyelids, rub rub.{p}

Then suddenly, Sanae turned her sleepy eyes my way.
What should I do?{p}I made a split-second decision.
Run away
Run over to her

I felt like this was bad, and I thought about running away.
But our eyes had met, right?
No point running away then.
Besides, she's my friend.
"Sanae!"
Without thinking, I grabbed her hand.
It was shockingly cold.
Just like a dead person's.
I almost let go without meaning to.
But then Sanae squeezed my hand tight.
I was about ready to cry.
"Reiko, stay like this.
Keep holding my hand, okay?"
She said it with blank, unfocused eyes.
She was looking at me, but her eyes seemed to go right through me, looking at something behind me.{p}

Feeling like I'd been hypnotized, I just nodded and did as she said.
Little by little, Sanae's hand got its warmth back.
Her eyes slowly came into focus too, and she came back to herself.
And then, all of a sudden, she hung her head.
I didn't know what to say either, so I kept quiet.
It was kind of awkward.
"...Reiko, did you see it?"
I was so startled.
I mean, out of nowhere, Sanae comes out with that.{p}I didn't know how to answer...
Tell her I saw it
Tell her I didn't see anything

I felt like she'd see through me if I lied...
So I answered honestly.
"What... was that?
Sanae, did you already know about it?"{p}

Sanae looked up at me from under her lashes, then hung her head again.
"...Yeah. That was my grandma."
"Your grandma? That wasn't you?"
"It wasn't me. It was Grandma.
Grandma died three years ago, you know.
And ever since, she's been inside me.
Sometimes she comes out like that."
Sanae said it with her head still hanging.
I didn't know what to say back.
"Grandpa's in here too.
And my dad's big sister, and my mom's dad, and all kinds of people are inside me."
Sanae told me that, too.
I just nodded without saying anything.
Somehow I felt like I shouldn't joke about it or make fun of her.
With a serious face,
"Yeah, I see, I see,"
is what I said.
"And Grandma and the others teach me all sorts of things.
Like stuff about tests, and tomorrow's weather, all kinds of things.
...Even what everyone thinks of me."
My heart skipped a beat.
If I thought anything weird, it would all get passed on to Sanae.
"...Don't be scared, okay?
Reiko, you're a good friend.
Please keep being my friend from now on, too."
I answered right away.
"Okay,"
I said.
Then, since P.E. still wasn't over, I said goodbye.
Sanae stayed behind, saying she'd keep resting in the classroom.{p}

See?
She's weird, right?
...Sanae and I are still good friends.
She's the same as ever, but she's a good kid.
Oh yeah, this is a secret, okay?
Since then, she's been telling me what's going to be on tests and stuff.
She says she asked her grandma.
And it's spot-on every time.
But it sounds too wild to be true, doesn't it?{p}Can you believe it?
I believe it
I don't believe it
I can't really say

Yeah, I figured.
You can't believe it unless you actually see it, huh?
So anyway, remember I said Sanae prays at lunch?
I wanted to know what she was mumbling about, so I snuck up close and listened.
And guess what she was saying?{p}

"My, my, what a tasty-looking lunch again today,"
and
"Ahh, I'm a lucky old fella, I am,"
that's the kind of stuff she was saying.
And it wasn't Sanae's voice, either.
It was somebody else's voice.
I thought Sanae might be doing an impression of someone, but that wasn't it.
When I listened closely, I could hear a bunch of voices at the same time.
Not just one voice. Lots of them were all chattering at once.
I peeked at Sanae's face.{p}

And then, guess what? Right at her slightly open mouth, I could see human faces.
Tiny human faces, like the heads of matchsticks.
There must have been about twenty of them.
And they were all staring hard at the lunch.
Those faces were each saying whatever they liked.
I froze up again.
Just then, Sanae suddenly grabbed my hand.{p}

Then she looked at me and smiled.
"Grandma just said something.
She says you're going to meet a {f:boy|girl} soon, Reiko.
That {f:boy|girl} is in a really dangerous position right now.
So she told me to tell you to be careful, Reiko.
Be careful, Reiko. Apparently that {f:boy|girl}'s name is {c}{f:|}."{p}

...And that's the end of my story.
{c}{f:|}.
Meeting you like this can't be a coincidence, can it?
I bet you don't believe it, but Sanae was giving a warning.
You've got some kind of secret, don't you?
Am I wrong?
Well, I don't know what it is.
But you'd better be careful.
I don't really know the details myself.
So, whose story is next?
I can't wait... Hee hee.{p}

Yeah.
So I quietly watched her for a while.
Thinking stuff like, if Sanae doesn't stop shaking, I'll have to go get the nurse.

Sanae kept on shaking and shaking.
But when I looked closer...
It didn't seem like she was shaking.
It was more like she was fiddling around with something under the blanket.
I got the feeling I'd seen something I wasn't supposed to, so I ducked out of sight a bit.
And then Sanae...

sat up all of a sudden and walked right out of the nurse's office.
With her face still pale.
I wondered where she could be going when she felt so sick, but...
I wanted to know what Sanae had been doing in the bed, so I checked the bed a little.
And from inside the pillowcase...{p}

...Want to know?
What'll you give me if I tell you?
Ahaha, kidding, kidding.
So, from inside the pillowcase, out came a little scrap of paper.
It looks like Sanae had been fiddling around under there to slip it in.{p}

On that scrap of paper was one word:
'Ketsu'
That's what was written on it.
Hey, what are you laughing at?
I was really scared when I saw that paper, you know.{p}I mean, 'Ketsu'...
It's 'ketsu' as in 'decide'
It's slang for 'butt', right?
I'm pretty sure there's an idol by that name...

It means 'ketsu' as in 'decide,' right?
Hiding the word 'decide' in a bed...
You'd think she was brooding over something, wouldn't you?
So I got worried and went looking for Sanae.{p}

I thought maybe she'd gone back to the classroom, or if she was that desperate, maybe she was on the roof, so I looked all over.
But she wasn't there.
She wasn't anywhere.
I was wandering up and down the hallway wondering what to do, when I heard a sound coming from the chemistry lab.

Clink, clunk... like that.
There wasn't any class in the chemistry lab at that hour.
Right away, I thought,
it might be Sanae.
Maybe Sanae, troubled by something, was looking through the chemical cabinet to take some deadly chemical from the lab.
So I quietly peeked in.{p}

It was Sanae, all right.
Sanae took a bottle of some kind of powder off the shelf...
She stuck her middle finger in the bottle, stirred it a little, and licked the powder off her finger.
Oh no!
I'd been watching with my breath held, so I missed my chance to stop her.
If that was poison, Sanae might die.
Then Sanae staggered out of the chemistry lab again and went off somewhere.{p}

I looked for the chemical Sanae had licked.
At the back of the chemical cabinet, where Sanae had been rummaging around, I looked for a bottle of that shape.
Inside the bottle was a brown powder...
It didn't have a label.{p}So what do you think I did?
Lick what's inside the bottle
Take the bottle to a teacher

It means 'butt,' right?
What would she put a word like that in a pillowcase for?
Kind of scary, don't you think?
Sanae was supposed to have come to the nurse's office because she felt sick, and she's slipping a scribble that says 'Ketsu' into the pillow...
Maybe she wants to dream about butts?
If that's true, nothing could be scarier, right?
.........
But that wasn't it.{p}

Ahaha...
Could you tell it wasn't that?
At the time, I was thinking,
(Butts, seriously...?)
but Sanae's face had been so pale that I got worried and went looking for her.{p}
